renovate

/REN-uh-vayt/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Renovate means to restore a building or other large structure to a good state of repair through major work, making it look newer and better.

The Okafor sisters spent two summers working to renovate the old wooden sailboat, sanding the hull and replacing every rotted plank.

Example

The Ruiz family spent all spring renovating their farmhouse kitchen, ripping out the sagging cabinets, leveling the crooked floor, and installing bright new counters.

The kitchen had fallen into disrepair, and the family repaired its structure and updated its look until it was in good condition again. Restoring a space to a solid, newer, better state is exactly what renovate means.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

remodel: Remodel means to change the structure or style of a space — knock out a wall, move the kitchen, reshape the layout. Renovate means restoring a structure to good repair through major work: it fixes and freshens what is there. Remodeling changes the design; renovating brings the existing design back.

refurbish: Refurbish means to brighten up and repair something so it looks and works like new — cleaning, repainting, replacing small parts. It is the lighter job. Renovate implies major structural work on a building or large structure: floors leveled, cabinets ripped out, rot replaced.

modernize: Modernize means to update something to current standards — new wiring, new fixtures, a contemporary look. It is about bringing things up to date. Renovate is about bringing them back to good condition, which can mean faithfully restoring an old look rather than updating anything.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

neglect: to fail to care for

ruin: to destroy the condition of

Where it sits · how deep into the structure work goes

redecorate → renovate → rebuild

redecorate vs. renovate: Redecorate is weaker than renovate; redecorating changes paint and curtains, while renovating repairs the structure itself.

rebuild vs. renovate: Rebuild is stronger than renovate; a renovated structure keeps its original bones, but a rebuilt one is torn down and constructed all over again.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-: again, back

Root — nov: new (from Latin novus)

Suffix — -ate: to make (verb-forming)

Put it together: Re- means again, nov comes from the Latin novus meaning new, and -ate forms a verb. So renovate literally means to make something new again.

Use the root in a new word: innovate: Engineers at the toy company are expected to innovate every season, and the patent plaques now fill a hallway.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / everyday

The go-to verb for fixing up buildings and rooms: renovate a house, a kitchen, or a stadium. It implies real repair work, so it is stronger than redecorate, which only changes surfaces like paint and furniture. Remember that people and reputations are rehabilitated, not renovated.
